turns.t: I've got this lump on my wrist, and I'm worried because I looked it up and it said it could be anything.
Let's have a look and talk it through. Which wrist is it?
The right one, on the back of the wrist. It's about the size of a grape.
When did you first notice it?
Three weeks ago, I think. It seems to have got a bit bigger.
Does it hurt?
Only when I bend my wrist back a lot, like when I do press-ups.
Does the size change during the day or after using the wrist?
It's bigger after I've been typing. Smaller in the morning.
Have you had a knock or an injury to it?
No, no injury.
Any tingling or numbness in the fingers?
No, nothing like that.
Do you use your hands a lot at work? ~
I'm a programmer. I'm typing all day. ~
Let me have a look. Put your hand on the table, palm down. ~
Like this?
This is a smooth, firm, rounded swelling, and it moves a little under the skin. It's not tender, and I can shine a light through it. ~
What is it, then? ~
This looks like a ganglion, a harmless sac of fluid that forms next to a tendon sheath.
Is it dangerous? Could it turn into something else? ~
No, it's not cancerous, and it doesn't turn into anything. ~
Do I need it removed? ~
Not unless it bothers you. They can disappear by themselves, over months, or even years. ~
Should I get it drained? ~
Draining often leads to it coming back. I'd leave it alone, unless it begins to hurt. ~
And I shouldn't hit it with a book? ~
Please don't. That old remedy can cause damage. ~
Okay. That's a relief. ~
If it gets painful, grows quickly, or you get numbness or weakness in the fingers, come back and we'll consider referral.
I will. Thank you, doctor. ~
